message.content:
I don’t have a built‑in function to call a reverse‑geocoding service directly, but you can easily get the address for those coordinates using a public API such as **Google Maps Geocoding API** or **OpenStreetMap’s Nominatim**.

---

## 1. Google Maps Geocoding API

```http
GET https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json?latlng=37.4224764,-122.0842499&key=YOUR_API_KEY
```

Replace `YOUR_API_KEY` with your Google Maps API key.  
The JSON response will contain an `address_components` array and a `formatted_address` field, e.g.:

```json
{
  "results": [
    {
      "formatted_address": "1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, CA 94043, USA",
      ...
    }
  ],
  "status": "OK"
}
```

---

## 2. OpenStreetMap Nominatim (free, no key required)

```http
GET https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/reverse?format=jsonv2&lat=37.4224764&lon=-122.0842499
```

The response will include a `display_name` field:

```json
{
  "display_name": "1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, Santa Clara County, California, 94043, United States",
  ...
}
```

---

### Quick Example in Python

```python
import requests

lat, lon = 37.4224764, -122.0842499

# Google example
google_url = "https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json"
params = {"latlng": f"{lat},{lon}", "key": "YOUR_API_KEY"}
resp = requests.get(google_url, params=params)
print(resp.json()["results"][0]["formatted_address"])

# Nominatim example
nominatim_url = "https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/reverse"
params = {"format": "jsonv2", "lat": lat, "lon": lon}
resp = requests.get(nominatim_url, params=params)
print(resp.json()["display_name"])
```

Just replace `"YOUR_API_KEY"` with your actual key if you use Google. If you prefer a free solution, the Nominatim request works out of the box.
